reviews.review:
[h1] I want to like it [/h1]
I really want to like this game. I really want to say that it's an amazing game with no issues what so ever, and in fact, it's not all that far away from being such a game. But unfortunately, every single time I play it for longer than 40, or 50 hours, I have to walk away from it. 

Then, a new update will be released that will somewhat get my interest, and I will come back, check what's changed, play against the latest enemies for about 50 hours, and leave again. 

[h1] Why? [/h1]

When you've "forgotten" all that's bad about it, it's easy to regain the same enthusiasm and the same enjoyment that you got out of it the first time you've played, but then, it only takes about 50 hours to start noticing all of the "odd things".

[h2] Odd things? [/h2]
[h3]Host disadvantage[/h3] - Being a host quite literally puts you at a disadvantage, because the AI will path find to you, and you specifically. Your stealth will not work 90% of the time. Your stratagems, even thrown 90 meters away from you, will instantly act as a beacon, to attract all of the enemy AI, no matter of which faction, to your location.

[h3]Invisible "walls" [/h3] - There are an insane amount of structures that will get you stuck either under or inside of other buildings, with your only choice being cooking a grenade, and respawning.

[h3]"Meta's" [/h3] - You want to fight this new enemy? - Here's the only 3 things that will hurt it. Have fun. Everything else you have is worthless, not just "harder", worthless. The game, actively forces the players to always use the same loadout, with the same stratagems and same weapons because it's not that they're effective, it's that they're the only viable way to play the game on the hardest difficulty.

[h3]Game breaking bugs that have been in the game since release [/h3] - Instead of fixing the game, with the objectives that get soft-locked and are impossible to complete, leading to some runs simply ending with failure not because of you doing something wrong, but because the game decided to simply not acknowledge that the buildings that you've destroyed were destroyed, or, in some instances, will lock out consoles with you being unable to do anything Arrowhead focuses on releasing war bonds, for a game that you've already paid for, and, those war bonds at most give you 3 or 4 useful items while costing approximately 20$ each. Now granted, you can very easily get the super credits, but it still feels wrong.

[h3]Misleading communications [/h3] Arrowhead often just "say things". There's seemingly no rhyme or reason to say those things, but they still do, they make posts, promises, and very often simply openly lie to their community. It's just odd. "We've not touched this thing, we swear" - "5 videos of players testing how it worked vs how it works now showing the changes." And many more things, including promising war bonds that never come because some other company paid them more for priority. It's just odd all around, there's no reason to just "say things".

[h1] My opinion [/h1]

In it's current state, the game is fine. You can enjoy it, and I will keep returning to it every few months each time there's something new added to it, but I can't recommend it for the life of me. It just feels like a game that had so much potential, has so many things, but ultimately falls down into the trap of most "extraction shooters" where, instead of allowing the players to just do what they want, they end up creating, possibly unintentionally an "only one right way to play" and it just defeats the purpose of having everything there is in the game.

What's the point of having all of those stratagems, if 90% of them simply are pointless against the enemies that have been turned into bullet sponges and can tank anything other than the 3 stratagems that work against them?

What's the point of having so many upgrades to your weapons, when the only gun you'll use is the one they buff?

What's the point of upgrading your ship modules, if none of the stratagems that you use are affected by half of those modules?

The game just feels like it threw away the "sandbox-y" feel that it had, where you could take any gun, any stratagem, and any armor, and instead chooses to hand-hold you through a very linear experience where you have to take every single step they want you to take if you want the game to be "easy". 

Ultimately, I don't want an easy game, I want to play the way I want to play, and use the weapons I want to use, but, when you get overrun because your gun simply doesn't do enough damage, and so the enemies just keep spawning and spawning, or, you run out of ammunition within two minutes and are forced to wait until the resupply is available again, unless you use this shiny gun, with this shiny stratagem, and this armor, and you'll be perfectly fine and won't even realize that the mission was hard at all.
if you don't play it I'll report you to the ministry of truth
